newsitem.title: CHINA: CROCODILE SHRS OFF AFTER TRADING RESUMES.
newsitem.headline: CROCODILE SHRS OFF AFTER TRADING RESUMES.

text.p: Shares of Crocodile Garments Ltd plunged after trading resumed on Friday following its parent Lai Sun Garment (International) Ltd's announcement that talks to sell its Crocodile shares had been terminated.
The stock dived about 21 percent to an early low of HK$0.88 before recovering to HK$0.95, down HK$0.16 in early trade on volume of 3.51 million shares worth HK$3.28 million.

Lai Sun Garment said earlier that a China-related third party that had expressed an interest to buy Crocodile shares from Lai Sun told the company that it had decided not to proceed with talks relating to the purchase of Crocodile shares.
Trading of shares in Lai Sun Garment and Crocodile resumed this morning after being suspended since Monday pending the announcement.
"Crocodile jumped steeply last Friday, and it's just profit taking after the news, which disappointed some investors," a local brokers said.
There was speculation that Lai Sun Garment could privatise Crocodile, its 54.93 percent unit, he said.
But Lai Sun Garment also said in a statement that it had no intention to privatise Crocodile. Lai Sun Garment shares were unchanged at HK$9.70 on Friday morning.
